stores.gdriveHelpSubtitle: Follow these steps to create an OAuth client ID and secret for Google Drive.
stores.gdriveHelpStep1: Open the Google Cloud Console and create a new project (or select an existing one).
stores.gdriveHelpStep2: Go to APIs & Services → Library, search for "Google Drive API", and click Enable.
stores.gdriveHelpStep3: Go to APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen. Choose External, fill in the app name and support email, then save.
stores.gdriveHelpStep4: While the app is in Testing mode, add the email that will connect the store as a test user: OAuth consent screen → Test users → Add users. Only approved testers can authorize the app (other accounts get "Error 403: access_denied").
stores.gdriveHelpStep5: Go to APIs & Services → Credentials → Create Credentials → OAuth client ID.
stores.gdriveHelpStep6: Set Application type to Web application, add the redirect URI below, then click Create.
stores.gdriveHelpStep7: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the dialog and paste them into the fields above.
stores.gdriveRedirectUriHint: Register this redirect URI in your Google Cloud Console OAuth client:
stores.localHelpSubtitle: Recommendations for attaching a local storage provider.
stores.localHelpTip1: Base Directory is the folder on disk where files are stored. Use a dedicated, persistent directory (e.g. a mounted disk or NAS), not a temporary folder. It is created automatically if it does not exist.
stores.localHelpTip2: Prefer an absolute path so the location is unambiguous regardless of where the server is started from.
stores.localHelpTip3: Public URL is optional. Fill it with your server's base URL (e.g. http://localhost:8081) to enable signed download links. Leave it empty if external access is not needed.
stores.localHelpTip4: Local storage is best for a single-server deployment. For multiple servers or ephemeral environments (Docker, Heroku), use S3 or Google Drive instead — the local disk is not shared between instances.
stores.localHelpTip5: To import files that already exist in a folder, attach a local store pointing at it and set Ingest Mode to 'poll'.
stores.credentialsSaved: Credentials are saved securely. Leave blank to keep existing values, or enter new ones to replace them.
stores.storageModeHint: Choose how files are distributed across your attached stores.
stores.storageModeCumulativeDesc: Each file is stored on one store. Writes pick the store with available quota; total capacity is the sum of all stores.
stores.storageModeReplicateDesc: Every file is copied to all writable stores. The primary store is the master; the rest are mirrors.
stores.syncDisabledCumulative: Replication is disabled in cumulative mode. Switch to Replicate to copy files across stores.

stores.s3ConnectSubtitle: Use the S3 API key with any S3-compatible tool such as the AWS CLI or rclone.
stores.s3ConnectStep1: Create an API key above, then copy the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key.
stores.s3ConnectStep2: Point your S3 client at the endpoint below using the key credentials, and use the bucket name (your workspace slug) for operations.
stores.s3ConnectFeatureFolders: Folders are created automatically when you upload to a key like docs/report.pdf — no separate mkdir step needed.
stores.s3ConnectFeatureList: List objects at the bucket root or filter with a prefix.
stores.s3ConnectFeatureUpload: Upload files with the AWS CLI, rclone, or any S3 SDK.
stores.s3ConnectFeatureDownload: Download files back to your machine.
stores.s3ConnectFeatureDelete: Delete objects when they are no longer needed.
stores.s3ConnectFeatureMultipart: Multipart uploads are supported for large files (create, upload part, complete, abort).
